config.specialists: neutral (0.5 + noise(0.05); bandit isolation, same as K5/K9/K10)

hypothesis: H1: combining per-cue gain vectors (K10: CueIndexedArbitrator) with baseline-free eligibility-trace updates (K9: SparseRewardArbitrator rule) beats EACH parent mechanism alone on cue-conditioned delayed_reward (the intersection of NR-A-006 and NR-A-007), and does not degrade either parent task. Mechanism: the cue in the input selects the context at t=0; the per-cue eligibility trace carries the delayed +1.0 back lambda^10 to the branch choice in the CORRECT cue's trace vector; the per-cue vector accumulates branch_cue credit across rewarded episodes while the baseline-free rule avoids the NR-A-006 universal decay (constant-0.5 baseline punishing every arm). The K10 arm's delta rule is predicted to decay under sparse reward (<= frozen, NR-A-006 mechanism); the K9 arm has no cue input and cannot distinguish cue episodes (replicates K9's structural failure).

new_modules.attention_cue_trace.py: CueTraceArbitrator subclasses CueIndexedArbitrator (attention_cue.py and attention.py UNTOUCHED). Per-context gain vectors (K10) + per-context eligibility traces. arbitrate(): decay+accumulate the ACTIVE context's traces. update_gains(): K9's baseline-free return-conditioned rule applied to the ACTIVE context's vector: if r = sum(utility.values()) != 0: gain_ctx[c] += lr * r * e_ctx[c] for e_ctx[c] > 0 (capped/floored); if r == 0: NO gain change (traces still decay in arbitrate). reward_baseline accepted for interface compatibility, DELIBERATELY UNUSED. With constant context this is the K9 code path; the tick wiring (arbitrator_cls + context_fn) is unchanged.
new_modules.cue_delayed_reward.py: CueDelayedReward env, NAME='cue_delayed_reward', VERSION='1.0.0', registered in flesh-pits/experiments/envs/__init__.py (additive; canonical envs untouched). ENV_INTERFACE v1.0.0 compliant: discrete 4-action space, obs {pos, branch, steps_left, cue}, state_hash over canonical state incl. rng.

null: H0: the combination fails >=1 gate on >=2/4 seeds -> record NR-A-012 (number reserved by the K10 prereg for a K10 failure, unused since K10 lifted; next free number). Predicted failure mechanism (stated before running): within EACH cue's trace vector, e_forward >> e_branch (10 forward steps vs 1 branch step per episode); the baseline-free rule saturates forward-per-cue to the 2.0 cap from shaping ticks alone; forward then wins the t=0 arbitration (a no-op there) with high probability; episodes truncate at 15 steps; the combination reproduces K9's structural failure per-cue. Cue-indexing would fix WHICH vector fails, not WHETHER a state-blind bandit learns branch-then-forward sequencing. This is a genuine test: a failed combination is a legitimate result.
preregistered_before: any implementation or execution of attention_cue_trace.py / cue_delayed_reward.py / k11_cue_trace_combination.py

arms.K10-arm: CueIndexedArbitrator, cue context, ORIGINAL delta rule (baseline 0.5)
arms.combined: CueTraceArbitrator (new module attention_cue_trace.py), cue context, baseline-free trace rule
arms.frozen: identical CueTraceArbitrator with frozen=True (all per-cue vectors pinned at 1.0; traces still update, harmless, no selection effect)

P1_main_intersection.context_fn_main: lambda obs: int(obs['cue'])  (cue in the input)
P1_main_intersection.env: cue_delayed_reward v1.0.0 (NEW: canonical delayed_reward mechanics LENGTH=10, MAX_STEPS=15, FORWARD_SHAPING=0.02, FINAL_REWARD=1.0, plus per-episode cue in {0,1} in the observation, constant within episode; correct branch = cue, documented fixed mapping; the agent is stimulus-blind with neutral specialists, so only per-cue gain vectors can encode the mapping)
P1_main_intersection.gate_note: G1 is expected to be the WEAK gate: the K10 arm is predicted to decay under sparse reward (NR-A-006 mechanism), possibly BELOW frozen, so G1 may pass trivially even if the combination ~= frozen. G2 (vs frozen) is the BINDING gate. A G1 pass with G2 fail = the combination adds nothing over chance.
P1_main_intersection.metric: per arm: total_reward(learned) per seed; ratios R_combined_X = total(combined)/total(arm X)
P1_main_intersection.verdict: MAIN WON iff G1 AND G2 both pass (>=3/4 each)

arms.combined: CueTraceArbitrator with CONSTANT context (context_fn = lambda obs: None) — must behave as the K9 trace path

P2_parent_delayed_reward.gate: non-degradation iff R >= 0.90 on >= 3/4 seeds (both expected bad, as in K9: 0.34-0.50 vs frozen; this is an equivalence control, not a win probe)
P2_parent_delayed_reward.metric: R = total(combined, constant ctx) / total(K9-arm) per seed
P2_parent_delayed_reward.protocol: K5 P1 identical (8 episodes x <=15 steps, same channels/capacity/hyperparameters)
P2_parent_delayed_reward.purpose: non-degradation on K9's parent task; equivalence control for the combination's trace path

arms.K10-arm: CueIndexedArbitrator, cue context, delta rule (head-to-head diagnostic, not a gate)
arms.combined: CueTraceArbitrator, cue context, baseline-free trace rule

P3_parent_changing_rule.gate: non-degradation iff R >= 1.30 on >= 3/4 seeds (the same lifting margin K10 beat)
P3_parent_changing_rule.metric: R = total(combined) / total(frozen) per seed; plus diagnostic total(combined)/total(K10-arm)
P3_parent_changing_rule.protocol: K10 B1 identical (12 episodes x 40 steps, channels a0/a1, capacity=2, cue context)
P3_parent_changing_rule.purpose: non-degradation on K10's parent task: the trace rule must not destroy the cue-adapter's proven win

verdict_rule: (i) MAIN WON (G1+G2) AND non-degradation (P2+P3) -> 'COMBINATION WINS'. (ii) MAIN WON but a parent gate fails -> 'PARTIAL: main win with parent-task trade-off', record which part degraded and how. (iii) MAIN fails -> NR-A-012 with the measured mechanism (which part failed and why). No post-hoc gate changes.
